content:
I often work on a branch where I need to use cache that is specific to that branch. One annoyance with this is that lake exe cache get first tries to download the cache for the master branch, which downloads almost nothing (because my branch differs from master), but this step takes a lot of time (about as much time as actually downloading the master cache). Here's what that looks like:

In particular the Downloaded 1 file(s) [attempted 8149/8149 = 100%, 0 KB/s] step takes about as much time as it takes to download 8149 files.

Does anyone know if this could be fixed? cc @Marcelo Lynch

The rationale here is that we always prefer 'official' ltars (the ones pushed to the master endpoint) and there is no way to check if they exist except by probing the whole set.

In the next few weeks I'll be working on refactoring the cache tool to recognize the "developer cache" scenario in a more principled way, so this is valuable feedback, I'll keep it in mind. This case should also improve in the medium term with lake cache, which should make for a smarter resolution of the 'downloadable set'.

(One immediate way I can think of making this faster is by pivoting to iterating per-file in this chain (master, fork cache) instead of per-link-in-the-chain across the whole set of files -- but you can see for instance how this would murk the log lines that are output, etc.; in any case, I'll post any improvements on this thread!)

@Jovan Gerbscheid an update on this

Part of the slowness was that the cache.mathlib.org endpoint was doing a few 'hops' between CloudFlare and Azure to support a smooth migration with Azure as a fallback. Enough time has passed with stability, so today I deployed a change in the endpoint so that a master cache read now goes to the CloudFlare bucket only.

With this, on my machine, lake exe cache get with a full miss went from 127 to 70 seconds.

Soon this sort of optimization will also reach the forks cache (some forks are still in older versions, so the fallback is still needed, but we will force a merge with master soon...)

Apart from this, I plan to increase the parallel transfers in the client itself. #44615 adds MATHLIB_CACHE_PARALLEL_MAX so I can try this out on CI with a higher value (today the default is 50, coming from curl).

But in fact you can change this setting today by adding this to your ~/.curlrc:

    parallel-max = 150

For me, doing this brings the full-miss case down to 30 seconds.
(The catch of #44615 is that if we start passing an explicit --max-parallel then .curlrc does not apply anymore, and the env var would be the only way to override)
What remains to be done before everything related to Azure is out of mathlib?

I believe both changes Marcelo mentioned upstream are now live on mathlib master: from a user's perspective, this is done. I don't know about internal clean-ups, but I trust Marcelo to perform these in due time.

This depends a bit on what you mean by "everything related to Azure is out of mathlib". Indeed, as Michael mentioned, mathlib developers (writing PRs) and downstream libraries are not interacting with Azure at all anymore (for cache purposes), for commits later than the one corresponding to #43308. Older versions of mathlib are still pulling the cache from Azure, which is still available.

As of #44832, merged today, we are also not uploading artifacts to Azure anymore, so people using / downstreams referencing versions of mathlib after this can't even use the 'legacy' Azure endpoint as a fallback.

Marcelo Lynch said in #mathlib4 > Failing to download cache is slow:

for commits older than the one corresponding to #43308

Do you mean for commits younger than ...?

By "out of mathlib" I mean that git grep zure .github/* and git grep zure Cache/* (accounting for both casings of Azure) should return zero results. Currently there are still some results, mostly azure-client-id: and azure-tenant-id: in the workflows
(It is misleading to just do git grep azure, because there is an author in the bibliography surnamed Demazure)

git grep zure Cache/* will give out hits because we are still supporting uploading to Azure in the cache tool, even if we don't use it anymore. I don't see any harm in this, I wasn't planning on removing it for now.

The results on git grep zure .github/* correspond to uses of Azure Key Vault in various CI workflows. This is not related to the cache. I want to replace this as well, but it's not a top priority right now.
